title: The Letter Mostafa Kandil Sent Two Months After Swvl Went Public
conflicts: First-half 2022 revenue: $40.7m (TechCrunch) or about $40m (Pakistan Today) vs $66m (TechCabal, Jan 2023); no H1 revenue figure used. Markets: 13 (TechCrunch, TechCabal, May 2022) vs 20 (Swvl's June 2022 statement); no total used. Listing price $10 vs $9.95; story says 'about $10'. Second layoff round '50% of remaining' (TechCrunch) vs 'over 50 per cent' (Wamda); story says half the rest. Volt Lines unwind dated December 2022 (Wamda) vs January 2023 filing (TechCabal); story says 'over the next year'. The 2023 net profit ($3.1m, TechCabal) leaned on subsidiary sales and Swvl said in 2026 it was still approaching operating breakeven, so the story says so rather than calling the turnaround complete.
notes: Country and region changed from the slate's Egypt / North Africa to United Arab Emirates / Middle East: Swvl was Dubai-based when Kandil made the cuts and the layoffs fell mostly on its Dubai and Pakistan offices; it remains Egyptian-founded with Egypt as its largest market. Editor may prefer to keep North Africa for rotation. Quote stance 'challenges'. Kandil's letter is quoted from TechCrunch's extract because Swvl's original page no longer loads.
